question: Can a class-balanced, CV-tuned LightGBM predict stale replica reads more accurately than a standard replica-lag threshold rule, using the same seeded simulated replicated store?
method: Seeded simulation of a replicated store with Poisson writes, per-replica lognormal propagation lags and random reads; reads labelled stale when the chosen replica lacks the latest write. Time-ordered train/test split fixed before fitting; tuning only by CV on training data; test set used once. Both models run with seeds 42, 43, 44.
metric_name: stale-class F1 on held-out test reads
baseline: Standard replica-lag threshold rule: flag a read as stale when the replica's time since last sync exceeds a threshold chosen by stratified CV F1 on the training set.
improved: Class-balanced LightGBM on per-read features (sync age, pending-update count, replica load, recent write rate, replica id); leaves and min child samples chosen by CV, and the decision threshold chosen on out-of-fold probabilities by CV F1 on the training set.
notes: Simulation is a stand-in, not a re-implementation of re:GRIDiT, and the paper reports no measurable model. Labels and features come from the simulator; pending updates are a replica-side queue count, so the task is not trivially solved. The split is time-ordered as the method specifies rather than stratified. Std is over model/CV seeds only; the simulated dataset is a single draw with a fixed seed.
